enonce_markdown: A stall owner in Bafoussam counted the customers who visited her stall on seven days: $8, 12, 5, 20, 9, 10, 6$. The mean number of customers per day is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The mean of a set of values is the sum of all the values divided by the number of values.

### Solution

Sum $= 8 + 12 + 5 + 20 + 9 + 10 + 6 = 70$ and the number of days is $7$.

Mean $= \dfrac{70}{7} = 10$ customers per day.

The other options come from other measures: $9$ is the median (middle value of $5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 20$), $15$ is the range ($20 - 5$) and $12.5$ is the mid-value of the smallest and largest numbers.

**Answer: 10.**

enonce_markdown: Eight students obtained the following marks out of 20 in a Mathematics test: $11, 14, 8, 17, 12, 9, 15, 13$. The median mark is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To find the median, arrange the values in order of size. With an even number of values, the median is the mean of the two middle values.

### Solution

Arranged in increasing order: $8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17$.

There are $8$ values, so the two middle values are the 4th and 5th: $12$ and $13$.

Median $= \dfrac{12 + 13}{2} = 12.5$.

Common errors: $12$ ignores the second middle value; $12.4$ is the mean ($\frac{99}{8} \approx 12.4$); $14.5$ comes from taking the middle of the unordered list ($17$ and $12$).

**Answer: 12.5.**

enonce_markdown:
Thirty pupils of a class in Ngaoundere were asked how many brothers and sisters they have. The results are shown in the table.

| Number of brothers and sisters | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of pupils | 5 | 9 | 8 | 6 | 2 |

The mean number of brothers and sisters per pupil is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For a frequency table, mean $= \dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$: multiply each value by its frequency, add the products, then divide by the total frequency.

### Solution

| $x$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f$ | 5 | 9 | 8 | 6 | 2 | 30 |
| $fx$ | 0 | 9 | 16 | 18 | 8 | 51 |

Mean $= \dfrac{51}{30} = 1.7$.

Common errors: $2$ is the middle value of the list $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ (it ignores the frequencies); $6$ is the mean of the frequencies ($\frac{30}{5}$); $10.2$ is $\frac{51}{5}$, dividing by the number of columns instead of the number of pupils.

**Answer: 1.7.**

enonce_markdown: The mean of six numbers is $8$. A seventh number is added to the list and the mean of the seven numbers becomes $9$. Find the seventh number.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Total of the values $=$ mean $\times$ number of values. The extra number is the difference between the new total and the old total.

### Solution

Total of the first six numbers $= 6 \times 8 = 48$.

Total of the seven numbers $= 7 \times 9 = 63$.

Seventh number $= 63 - 48 = 15$.

Check: $\dfrac{48 + 15}{7} = \dfrac{63}{7} = 9$.

**Answer: the seventh number is 15.**

enonce_markdown: A survey was carried out among $240$ pupils on how they travel to school. $60$ walk, $90$ use a motorbike taxi and the rest go by bus. The results are to be shown in a pie chart. The angle of the sector for motorbike taxi is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

In a pie chart, the angle of a sector is $\dfrac{\text{frequency of the item}}{\text{total frequency}} \times 360^\circ$.

### Solution

Angle for motorbike taxi $= \dfrac{90}{240} \times 360^\circ = 135^\circ$.

Check: walking gives $\dfrac{60}{240} \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ$ and bus ($240 - 60 - 90 = 90$ pupils) gives $\dfrac{90}{240} \times 360^\circ = 135^\circ$, and $90^\circ + 135^\circ + 135^\circ = 360^\circ$.

Common errors: $90^\circ$ uses the number of pupils directly as an angle; $37.5^\circ$ is the percentage ($37.5\%$) not converted into degrees; $60^\circ$ is the number of walkers used as an angle.

**Answer: 135°.**

enonce_markdown:
The table shows the time $t$ minutes taken by $30$ pupils to walk to school.

| Time $t$ (minutes) | $0 < t \le 10$ | $10 < t \le 20$ | $20 < t \le 30$ | $30 < t \le 40$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of pupils | 4 | 9 | 12 | 5 |

(a) State the modal class.

(b) Calculate an estimate of the mean time taken.

(c) Calculate the percentage of the pupils who took more than $20$ minutes. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For grouped data, the modal class is the class with the highest frequency. To estimate the mean, use the mid-value of each class: mean $\approx \dfrac{\sum f x}{\sum f}$ where $x$ is the class mid-value.

### Solution

**(a)** The highest frequency is $12$, so the modal class is $20 < t \le 30$.

**(b)** Mid-values: $5, 15, 25, 35$.

| Mid-value $x$ | 5 | 15 | 25 | 35 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f$ | 4 | 9 | 12 | 5 | 30 |
| $fx$ | 20 | 135 | 300 | 175 | 630 |

Estimated mean $= \dfrac{630}{30} = 21$ minutes.

**(c)** Pupils who took more than $20$ minutes: $12 + 5 = 17$.

Percentage $= \dfrac{17}{30} \times 100 = 56.7\%$ (1 d.p.).

**Answers: (a) $20 < t \le 30$; (b) 21 minutes; (c) 56.7%.**
